parts:
Hi Sophia,

Robert (see below) has something working connecting Stan to Stata and was looking for the right person to share code with. Are any of your people actively working on this? I have Stata 12 for Linux installed on my laptop if I can be of help testing.

Ben

From: Grant, Robert L <Robert...@sgul.kingston.ac.uk>
Date: Fri, Mar 13, 2015 at 12:06 PM
Subject: Stata command for calling Stan
To: "bg2...@columbia.edu" <bg2...@columbia.edu>, "goodri...@gmail.com" <goodri...@gmail.com>


Dear Ben


We met very briefly at JSM last year after your talk on Stan, when I came up and said I had been working on a Stata program for calling Stan. Ever since then I've felt bad that I haven't done anything with it but lots of projects leapfrogged (ha!). Anyway, I've just got round to pulling it together into one place. So I would be very happy to help in any way I can if the Stan team are still doing some work on a Stata interface. Would you like to put me in touch with whoever's leading on that and I can share the code with them?


Thanks!

Robert


--

   St George's, University of London & Kingston University

Robert:

Thanks! We would very much like to have a Stata interface
for Stan.

Would you mind working in GitHub on stan-dev? If so, we should
set up a GitHub repo, such as

stan-dev/statastan

or however you want to name it. I guessed it'd be spell corrected
to "statistician", but Google disagrees:

Did you mean: statesman statscan statisten status tan

We also need a name, such as

StataStan

or however you want to name it. Then we can list it on our home page.

It would also need an explicit license if we're going to redistribute.
I strongly prefer the most liberal (in the sense of fewer restrictions,
not most "left") license compatible with Stata.

We can give you (Robert Grant) push permission on the repo and either
take the project over from you to manage or let you manage it.

Our dev process is here:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki

including tips for using GitHub. Before you panic, we've been much laxer in
enforcing the process outside of stan-dev/stan and stan-dev/cmdstan.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: missing data (vs. parameters) in BUGS/JAGS
parts:
What does BUGS/JAGS do if you have missing non-modeled
parameters. That is, if I have a regression and have
missing predictors, but no distribution given to the predictors.

For example, what if I have the model

sigma ~ cauchy(0,2.5)
beta ~ cauchy(0,2.5)
alpha ~ cauchy(0,2.5)
for (n in 1:N)
y[n] ~ normal(alpha + beta * x, sigma)

and pass in data where some of the x are NA?
It'd gripe and fail to run, right? At least that's what
I hope it would do.

That is, BUGS/JAGS don't handle missing data per se,
only missing parameters, using Andrew's definitions of
parameter vs. data from BDA 1:1.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: missing data (vs. parameters) in BUGS/JAGS
parts:
On Wednesday, March 18, 2015 at 7:11:24 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
What does BUGS/JAGS do if you have missing non-modeled
parameters.  That is, if I have a regression and have
missing predictors, but no distribution given to the predictors.

I think it would fail due to a lack of a proper prior on the unknown values of x.

See the appendix of http://www.jos.nu/Articles/abstract.asp?article=282279 for how someone is supposed to do it in WinBUGS.

Ben

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stata command for calling Stan
parts:
Hi Robert,

For StataStan (or however you want to capitalize it), you're free to
manage it how you'd like. With that said:
- when tagging a release version, it should match Stan's version. For
example, when RStan uses Stan v2.6.0, then RStan's version is 2.6.0.
If RStan releases a patch version based on Stan 2.6.0, then RStan's
version is 2.6.0.1.
- for most of our repositories, we've made the default branch
`develop` and let the `master` branch be the latest tagged branch

More below:

On Tue, Mar 24, 2015 at 6:00 AM, Robert Grant <rober...@live.com> wrote:
> Thanks Daniel and other stan-devs
>
> I've been looking over the developers' Github policy before charging ahead
> and making a mess. Is there any preferred approach for the initial commit,
> i.e. labelling it in some way, immediately branching it into develop?

We tend to work in branches and use pull requests to manage when
things get merged into develop. It's a little heavy handed to start,
but it does provide some stability in the code base.

> I was thinking of asking for Stata users (on statalist.org) to alpha-test it on
> different platforms and versions, so I might add more detail than other
> repos have into README about installing CmdStan for beginners, e.g. dealing
> with 32-bit Windows. We can pare that back in due course.

That works. You can either tag alpha versions in git or provide
different branches. There shouldn't be a problem doing any of that.



Hopefully some of that's helpful. If you run into any trouble, email
us, especially if you're stuck on something specific that we can help
with.



Daniel

parts: That's interesting. They have written a Gibbs and M-H sampler with a limited range of distributions. I suspect it will run faster than BUGS/JAGS by virtue of their speedy matrix language Mata, but still get whupped by Stan in the usual situations. Anyway, I just pushed the first StataStan to Github, which I'll announce separately.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: missing data (vs. parameters) in BUGS/JAGS
parts:
> On Apr 8, 2015, at 3:58 AM, Robert Grant <rober...@live.com> wrote:
>
> That's interesting. They have written a Gibbs and M-H sampler with a limited range of distributions. I suspect it will run faster than BUGS/JAGS by virtue of their speedy matrix language Mata,

Where's the matrix processing? Are the models going to be
interpreted or compiled?

The usual bottleneck for random-walk M-H is the density
evaluation and the usual bottleneck for Gibbs is the conditional
sampling. Neither of these involve matrices except for some
multivariate things, and for that, JAGS at least uses the
R libs, which are themselves based on fast underlying matrix ops.

- Bob
